content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes or positive sentiment, especially when sentiment is >0.10; reduce forecast peak by 5–15%.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.30) or after sharp declines; add 3–8% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overreact to recent sentiment shifts; adjust by smoothing 3–5 day moving average of true values before forecasting.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.20 or more), reduce forecast volatility by 20–40% to avoid overfitting to noise.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid forecasting >15% above 30-day moving average unless sentiment is >0.40; otherwise, cap at 10% above to prevent overshoot.
